findings.summary: Single-issue ship has no second operand; pairwise score is undefined for a lone issue. Reduction = best score vs open same-milestone siblings. Faithful to viafera rubric but must distinguish 'no siblings to correlate' (neutral info) from 'siblings exist but all below threshold' (real low-affinity warning) to avoid warning fatigue on milestone-less projects.
gh fetch can fail/be offline/repo not on GitHub; affinity computation must degrade to an 'affinity unavailable' advisory and NEVER throw or block the ship (issue: warning-only, non-blocking).

Dead-code / always-on risk: scorer must print at least the affinity header on EVERY ship invocation, never gated behind any --option or behind 'siblings.length>0'. Adversarial verifier must confirm declared->computed->printed with no option guard.

Scope-leak check: reading siblings to SCORE is the scorer scaffolding, not batch ORCHESTRATION (#1263 = one sub-agent per issue + batch-report) nor the dispatch matrix (#1267). Keep the gh adapter read-only + capped; expose scoreAffinity/computeAffinityReport so #1263/#1267 reuse it. No orchestration logic added.

Re-derivation vs verbatim copy: viafera rubric is prose in a skill .md (start-task §7.3), not code; arbiter port is an original pure TS function with the same integer weights/threshold. No verbatim text copied.

runTaskShip is pure/synchronous and shared with #1260/#1263/#1267 lanes; doing affinity I/O inside it maximizes merge-conflict blast radius. Keep affinity in the cli.ts ship .action() wrapper; leave runTaskShip untouched.

note: All findings are design-guardrails folded into the plan (honest single-issue reduction, graceful degradation, always-on print, pure runTaskShip). No CRITICAL plan rework required.
